sections.html:
Sellers can list with an agent, sell on their own or accept a cash offer. The quickest of the three is usually the buyer who doesn't need a lender. Buckeye has nearly 30 master-planned communities in play, so find out early whether yours adds rules or fees to a sale.

  • Ask whether your community has an HOA, a community facilities district or a transfer fee, and collect the documents.
  • Ask each buyer for a written closing date and a written list of seller costs.
  • Keep copies of permits for pools, solar, fences and additions.

Buckeye had an estimated 125,445 residents on July 1, 2025, a 37.1 percent jump from 91,502 in April 2020. Owners live in 86.0 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $419,800.

Occupied master-planned communities include Verrado, Sundance, Tartesso, Festival Ranch, Sienna Hills, Westpark and Riata West. Others, such as Teravalis, which is planned for nearly 300,000 residents, are still unbuilt. Because so many sellers are in the same kind of neighborhood, a buyer will compare your price and your community's fees with the homes around you.

Skyline Regional Park, an 8,700 acre mountain preserve in the southern White Tank Mountains, and Buckeye Hills Regional Park, seven miles south of downtown on State Route 85, are the large outdoor draws. If your home is near either, say so in the listing. Schools come from several districts, so confirm which one serves your address before you describe it to a buyer.

Start with the city's Permit Center, part of Development Services. The department's phone number is 623-349-6200. The city warns that scammers send fake invoices from addresses ending in @usa.com, while the official domain is @buckeyeaz.gov. If an invoice for a permit or fee shows up unexpectedly, confirm it by phone before paying.

Ask the Permit Center whether a past project on your property, such as a pool, patio cover, solar panels or fence, was permitted and closed out. Ask the Business Licenses office what applies to renting the house before you sell, including the transaction privilege tax license questions on its Residential Rental Properties FAQ page. For nightly rentals, ask what the city requires at your address.

  • Find out whether past pool, solar, fence or patio work was permitted and closed.
  • Learn which rental licenses apply if you lease before you sell.
  • Verify any unexpected invoice by phone before you pay it.

sections.h2: Taxes and recording for a Buckeye sale
sections.html:
Buckeye is in Maricopa County, so the Maricopa Treasurer bills your property taxes, usually in two installments. Under A.R.S. 42-18052, the first half is due October 1 and delinquent after November 1, and the second half is due the next March 1 and delinquent after May 1. The county calendar gives December 31 as the last day to pay the full year without interest. If a mortgage company pays your taxes, check that the next installment is covered before closing.

The Maricopa County Recorder charges $30 to record most documents. The Arizona Department of Revenue requires an Affidavit of Property Value with a deed unless an A.R.S. 11-1134 exemption applies, and exempt deeds carry a notation such as A.R.S. 11-1134 B3. If your appraisal looks off, a real property owner has 60 days from the Notice of Value to appeal to the county assessor.

Copies of a recorded document cost $1 a page, and certification adds $3 per document. Ask your title company to order a copy of the recorded deed after closing, so you hold proof of the date and the parcel number.

sections.h2: What a sale looks like step by step
sections.html:
The sequence is short once the paperwork is in hand. You gather HOA or community documents and permit copies. You collect offers with closing dates and seller costs in writing. You sign with one buyer, and the title company checks the Maricopa County tax balance, prepares the deed and the Affidavit of Property Value, and records the deed. Without a lender in the middle, a cash buyer has no loan approval to wait on, which is where most of the time is saved.

If your community has a transfer fee or a community facilities district, ask for the documents now. A buyer sees those charges at the same moment you do, and a quick answer keeps the date you agreed on. If a mortgage company pays your taxes, that is one more place a payoff or a paid-through date has to be confirmed before closing.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Buckeye?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $419,800 for 2020 to 2024. The median gross rent over the same period was $1,963.

faqs.q: When are Maricopa County property taxes due for a Buckeye home?
faqs.a: The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after November 1. The second half is due March 1 and delinquent after May 1. Paying the full year by December 31 avoids interest.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed for a Buckeye sale?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder charges $30 for most documents. A completed Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption notation on the deed has to accompany it.

faqs.q: Which phone number should I use for Buckeye permit questions?
faqs.a: The city's Development Services department answers at 623-349-6200. Confirm any invoice or fee with that number before paying it.

faqs.q: What should I ask about before selling in a master-planned community?
faqs.a: Ask whether the community has an HOA, a community facilities district or a transfer fee, and collect the documents. Buyers will want to see them, and they may add costs to the sale.
